promptLatex: A circle with centre $O$ has radius $5$, and a point $P$ lies $13$ units from $O$. A secant from $P$ meets the circle at $A$ and then $B$, and a tangent from $P$ touches the circle at $T$. If $PA = 9$, what is $PB$, in units?
hintLatex: The radius to the point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent.
The tangent length squared equals the product of the two segments cut off by the secant.
solutionLatex:
At the point of tangency the radius $OT$ is perpendicular to the tangent $PT$, so triangle $OPT$ is right-angled at $T$ with hypotenuse $OP = 13$ and leg $OT = 5$.

The Pythagorean theorem gives $PT^{2} = 13^{2} - 5^{2} = 169 - 25 = 144$, so $PT = 12$.

The tangent and the secant come from the same external point, so $PT^{2} = PA \cdot PB$. That gives $144 = 9 \cdot PB$, hence $PB = 16$. The inside piece is $16 - 9 = 7$, which is shorter than the diameter $10$, as any chord must be.
